To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the Great Crisis was not the result of the actions of individuals, but rather the result of a set of habits that were already in place before the crisis.
the intensification of neoliberalism is due to the falsified and fluid agency and identity of the neoliberal individual.
within neoliberalism an individual's agency is falsified and identity is fluid.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the relationship between agency, identity, and the Great Recession.
the ways in which neoliberal ideology has altered the ways in which we understand our identities and agency.
the role played by agency and identity in neoliberalism and how they have contributed to the intensification of neoliberalism.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
within neoliberalism the habituating tools, which are used to create and sustain the neoliberal project, are commodity fetishism, the conspicuous consumption of luxury goods, and moral panic.

the intensification of neoliberalism, and its subsequent intensification of the Great Crisis, is due in part to its ability to manipulate the habits of thought of the masses through the use of commodity fetishism and conspicuous consumption.
the Great Crisis has been a catalyst in furthering the neoliberal project.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Great Crisis of 2007-09 has had an effect on neoliberalism, but not as much as we may have expected.
the Veblen approach is a useful tool to analyze the Great Crisis and the neoliberal project.
the Veblenians' theory of habit is the most appropriate lens to view agency and identity within neoliberalism, as well as the Great Recession.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Great Crisis has not only intensified the neoliberal project but that it has done so by further falsifying the agency and identity of the individual.
the neoliberal project has not only intensified, but also become more entrenched within the fabric of our social and economic institutions.
neoliberalism, as a project, is not only unsustainable but also fundamentally unsustainable.
